name: Shopify
summary: Shopify builds commerce software for merchants, and its interviews are known for 'The Life Story', a conversation with a recruiter about the choices, wins and setbacks in your career, which Shopify describes on its careers site. For engineering roles, candidates commonly report a coding exercise, a pair-programming session and a technical deep dive into a past project; other crafts often have a craft assessment and team interviews.
rounds: 'Life story' conversation about your path and choices
looks_for: Impact, readiness, trust, engagement and self-awareness (the traits Shopify's engineering blog says the Life Story looks for)

questions.text: Walk me through your life story: the big choices and why you made them.
covers: Three or four turning points, in order, not a list of every job
Why you made each choice and what you learned from it
How the path leads to this role at Shopify

questions.text: Tell me about a time things changed fast at work. What did you do?
covers: What changed and how little notice you had
How you re-planned and what you let go of
The result, and what you'd do the same way next time

questions.text: Who are Shopify's merchants, and what would you build for them?
covers: The range of merchants, from first-time sellers to large brands
One specific merchant problem, such as selling across channels or managing stock
What you'd build first and how you'd know it helped merchants sell more

questions.text: Tell me about one of your bruises: a decision that went wrong and what you learned from it.
covers: A real mistake, owned plainly
What you saw at the time and what you missed
What you do differently now, with an example

questions.text: Tell me about the achievement you're proudest of. What impact did it have, and on whom?
covers: Why it was hard and what your part was
The impact on users, customers or the team, with a number if you have one
Why it matters to you more than other wins

questions.text: Tell me about a time you taught yourself something hard because the work needed it.
covers: What you had to learn and why it couldn't wait
How you learned it: building, reading, asking people
What you delivered and how you keep learning now

questions.text: Walk me through a project you know well: the architecture, the trade-offs you made and what you'd do differently.
covers: The business goal and a short picture of the architecture
Two or three decisions, the options you rejected and why
What broke or surprised you, and what you'd change now

questions.text: In a pair-programming session, how do you share your thinking with your partner? Talk me through how you'd start a new task.
covers: Restating the task and asking clarifying questions first
Thinking aloud, starting simple and running code early
Edge cases, tests, and inviting your partner's ideas

questions.text: How would you design a checkout that keeps working when a merchant's flash sale brings ten times the usual traffic?
covers: Where the load lands: product pages, carts, inventory, payments
Queues, caching and limits that protect the system without losing orders
Not overselling stock, and what shoppers see when things slow down

questions.text: A merchant says orders stopped appearing in their admin an hour ago. How would you investigate?
covers: Checking scope first: one merchant or many, since when
Following an order through the system using logs and metrics
Keeping the merchant updated and fixing the cause, not just the symptom

questions.text: How would you design inventory tracking that keeps stock counts right across an online store and a physical shop?
covers: One source of truth for stock and how each channel updates it
Handling two sales of the last item at the same moment
What happens when a shop's connection drops, and how counts are reconciled

questions.text: Why Shopify, and what does making commerce better for everyone mean to you?
covers: A reason tied to merchants and the products, not only the brand
A personal link: a business you know, a store you built, a problem you saw
The kind of work you want to do here

questions.text: What do you want to learn in your next role, and how will you know you're growing?
covers: One or two specific skills, not a general wish to grow
How you plan to build them and the support you'd look for
A sign of progress you'd check after a year

tips: For the life-story round, explain why you made each choice, not just what you did.
Before the Life Story, list your turning points, proudest wins and hardest moments; Shopify says it wants to hear about the trophies and the bruises.
In pair programming, think aloud and ask your partner questions. Shopify's engineering blog says a well-reasoned incomplete solution beats a fragile finished one.
For the technical deep dive, pick a project with real business trade-offs rather than a solo side project, and treat it as a conversation.
Try the product as a merchant would, for example by setting up a test store, so you can talk about it from experience.

sources.title: Shopify careers FAQ: the interview process (shopify.com)
